findings.location: architecture/i05-gate-channel-v3-supplement/README.md, last paragraph ('The order of failures inside the queue is not observable in the model's outputs (a clean failure leaves no record and failures fall on consecutive attempts), so no vector pins it.')
findings.finding: The claim is false. Each storage-failure cascade consumes only a bounded number of record attempts (the failed record, then INVALIDATED, then DENIED if an action is armed). So the queued failures can split across two events, and GENERATION_STATUS returns journalDigest between them. Probe in the pinned v3 model (scripts/order_probe.py in my work dir): GENERATION_STATUS, BIND_EXECUTION, STORAGE_FAIL_NEXT, STORAGE_FAIL_NEXT {torn: true}, STORAGE_FAIL_AFTER {after: 0}, ARM_ACTION, GENERATION_STATUS, CLOSE_GENERATION, GATE_RESTART. Results: ARM_ACTION is refused STORAGE_FAILURE in both variants. The second GENERATION_STATUS reports journalDigest sha256:ec2b97d3... under the model (AFTER failure appended behind the NEXT failures, so the torn NEXT falls inside ARM's cascade) and sha256:f505dbf8... under the prepend variant (the torn NEXT falls at the restart). The final snapshots are equal. A small systematic search with a status read between failure runs found 4 distinguishing cases in 147. The author's search used tails without that read. Since this README says the order is unobservable, an R10 implementation could take either order and still pass every vector, while diverging from the model on such event sequences.
findings.requiredChange: Replace the sentence with an accurate one. For example: the order is not observable in S01-S05; it is observable through a journalDigest read between two failure runs, which no vector pins; model-defined: an AFTER failure is appended behind the pending NEXT failures. Or add a transcript like the probe that pins the order, and list it as model-defined.

findings.finding: (a) 'No graph has harness-engineering consuming the operator, so this edge keeps every unconditional graph acyclic' still rules out only a direct back-edge. A cycle could also pass through another repository. The sufficient fact, which holds today, is that harness-engineering consumes no repository in any graph (repositories.yaml lists no edge with it as consumer). The rule defers to the layer, which must compute acyclicity over repositories.yaml plus the registry edges. (b) The notArtifacts reason says 'no harness-onion byte is in R10', which is literally false: R10 holds the three byte-identical HE-000 transport files. It means that no byte of the classifier or its inputs is in R10.
findings.requiredChange: (a) State that harness-engineering consumes no repository in any graph (or simply that the layer computes acyclicity). (b) Say that no byte of the classifier or its inputs is in R10.
